stories.summary:
The dreaded Chefs come into Highmark on Thanksgiving to take on the Bills.  Will this game follow the pattern of the Bills beating the Chefs in the regular season?  Or will Pat the Rat rise up and smite the Bills in a regular season game?



	 



	I reserve my answers to those questions for later.  I am really worried about the Chefs this week.  They appear to have their best team in years.  The only saving grace is that the Bills seemed to be bending over backwards to save their guys for the Chefs game.  Josh had no rushes, Bernard only played 50% of the D snaps.  The D played the replacements most of the 4th QTR, Tre' White, et al.  I think the Bills used the Fish as a mini-bye week to get ready for the short prep week up to Thanksgiving.

stories.title: Bills Defense is now Top 10
stories.summary:
Don't look now (because Sunday stats aren't up yet), but the Bills defense is now right around tenth in the league in both yards allowed per game and points allowed per game. 



	 



	Now, I know lots of people will say the Bills did it on the backs, literally, of a bunch of lousy teams with no quarterbacks, but that argument only goes so far. Every team is playing some collection of lousy teams with no quarterbacks. The fact is that so far this season, parity hasn't dominated. The league is much about the haves and the have nots, and everyone is playing some have nots. 



	 



	It's more important to notice two things.  First, we always knew the defense was going to be a work in progress, because it was a new coordinator and a new scheme. I expected the defense to improve during the season, and there is no question that it has. We're not seeing DBs looking at each other wondering who's going where. Lineman line up correctly. Blitzes are now nicely disguised. 



	 



	Second, the Bills have a first-class defensive lineup. Hooker and Bishop already are showing what two good safeties who communicate can do. The Bills are deep at corner, with Benford, IGB, Hairston, and White. Hancock quickly has shown that he isn't a liability on the field, and the same with Hamlin. Bills are a little thin at linebacker, but Bernard and Williams have been pretty solid, Elarms-Orr has shown he fits in, and now Shaq Thompson is getting on the field and getting some tackles. And the defensive line is playing well, with some nice plays being made by Carter and Landon Jackson behind the studs the Bills start. 



	 



	This is becoming a good defense. It needs to make a few standout performances down the stretch, but it no longer requires a miracle.

stories.title: Allen, Passing Game, and Offensive Play Calling
stories.summary:
The team is stacking wins and Allen and Cook have combined for 20 rushing TD's or more than 2 per game!



	 



	I love that we have a top running game for the playoffs.



	 



	Naturally, when your team has continuity on the OL and an elite running game, the passing game is affected/impacted.



	 



	I am completely fine with the running game making us more balanced.



	
	For those who know more about offensive schemes and philosophies, is our offensive play calling much different in the passing game than the past 3-4 years?



	 



	Is Allen regressing or past his peak as a passer?



	 



	Does the passing game just look and feel different because we have 3-4 guys who will get you 40-50 yards rather than 1 guy who may get a 100 yards?



	 



	I am curious if the passing game has been changing to allow the running game to take more time off the clock and help a younger and transitioning defense.



	 



	The answers to these questions are all probably "yes" to some degree.



	 



	Wondering about the passing game and play calling going forward.
